user.title: Zeekr account access
user.description:
Choose the login channel for this config entry — **this decides whether the car can be controlled**:

- **Phone + verification code**: **status *and* control**. You only type a phone number and the SMS code; the integration then exchanges the app login for the same GRIC credentials the mobile app uses. One value still has to be supplied by hand (a 44-character identifier that the app only computes in memory) — see the README section "How to obtain it".
- **GRIC token**: **status *and* control**, seeded from a token you capture yourself, plus the same identifier. Use this when the phone login is not an option (no SMS access, or you already have the token).
- **SMS verification code (+86)**: **vehicle status only** (battery, range, location, lock/door state…). **No control** — the gateway refuses every command interface for this token generation (`079001`), and the legacy fallback pipe answers "success" without executing anything. Logging in as the car's owner makes no difference.

{detail}

gric.title: GRIC token access (status + control)
gric.description:
This channel can read vehicle status *and* send control commands. It needs two values, both taken from **the same controllable Zeekr app session on one phone**:

1. **refreshToken** — from the **response body** of the app's `POST gric-api.geely.com/ms-midground-user/api/v1.0/user/auth/refresh/token`, field `data.refreshToken` (a ~900-character JWT starting with `eyJ`; do not paste the longer `accessToken`).
2. **x-vehicle-identifier** — the 44-character base64 (ends with `=`) in the **request headers** of any `gric-*.geely.com` request. It is computed inside the app's runtime only: it is not stored on the phone and cannot be derived offline.

Step-by-step capture instructions (capture app / mitmproxy / rooted phone) are in the README section "How to obtain both values".
Note: tokens are single-session — once saved, Home Assistant exchanges them for a new pair and the phone session is signed out. That is expected.
{detail}

gric_ident.title: One last value: the vehicle identifier
gric_ident.description:
Signed in, and the control-capable credentials are in place for **{vin}**.

The last value, `x-vehicle-identifier`, cannot be computed by anyone: the app derives it in memory from a key that only exists inside its native library, and it is never stored on the phone nor returned by the server. It has to be copied once from a real request:

1. Capture the app's HTTPS traffic (mitmproxy / LSPosed + a capture app / a proxy on your router).
2. Open the car in the app so a request to `gric-zhf-api.geely.com` is sent.
3. From that request's **headers**, copy `x-vehicle-identifier` — 44 characters of base64 ending with `=`.

It is bound to the car, not to the account: capture it once and it keeps working, even after switching phones or accounts. A wrong value is rejected immediately (`00A06`), never silently.
{detail}
